title: DR1 lists the user's own notifications however long ago they were made; the frontend dashboard is scoped to the browser session against the stub and to nothing at all against the real backend.

controls.text: You have not started any notifications in this session.

finding.frontend: The frontend's empty dashboard says so itself: "You have not started any notifications in this session." (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/copy/copy.en.js:56, rendered at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/dashboard/template.njk:157-159). The dashboard asks for a list of the journey ids this session happens to remember, not a list of the user's notifications: src/server/app/engine/journey.js:92-119 reads the ids out of the session store and passes them to the list query as a filter, and they live there for the life of the session (src/server/app/services/persistence/session/real.js:6-24). Which notifications that actually produces depends on which store is behind it, and neither answer is the user's own. Against the stub, the filter is applied (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:15-23), so a user who signs out, comes back tomorrow, or opens the service on a second device meets an empty dashboard whatever they created or submitted before — that is the captured behaviour. Against the real backend the filter is silently dropped: the list read sends only page, sort and reference number (src/server/app/services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:24-39), so the dashboard shows every notification the service holds, including other people's.
finding.prototype: DR1 heads the list "My notifications" and shows four notifications belonging to the user, three of them submitted days earlier with an arrival date in the future and a status the authority has since set (app/views/dashboard.html:80-294). Two of the four read "Submitted action required", a state that can only be reached after the user has gone away and come back. DR1's status filter offers Approved, Rejected and Complete on the same terms, so the list is required to survive the session that created it.
finding.difference: The dashboard has to list the notifications belonging to the signed-in user or their organisation — not the ones this browser session happens to remember, and not everything the service holds. That means the list read stops filtering on session-held journey ids and asks the backend for the caller's notifications instead, which needs the list endpoint to support an owner-scoped query and the records to carry an owner. Do this before the status work and the filter work: filtering a session's handful of drafts by status or arrival date has little to filter. The real adapter dropping the session filter is a separate defect from the parity gap and wants raising on its own, but the fix here supersedes it — an owner-scoped read is what both need.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding the frontend's list read scoped to the signed-in user or their organisation: an owner or organisation parameter in the query the real adapter sends to the notifications endpoint, rather than page, sort and reference number alone.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (fe-dashboard-empty.html:159 renders the sentence about this session; dr1-dashboard.html:701-861 renders four cards, three of them submitted days earlier with a status the authority has since set, two of those reading "Submitted action required") and the fe-dashboard-populated and dr1-dashboard-filters-open screenshots. Followed the claim into the source rather than accepting the empty-state copy as proof of it, and the substance holds but the mechanism was wrong in a way that matters — see correction. Traced engine/journey.js:96 to session.knownJourneyIds, then services/persistence/session/real.js:6-9 to request.yar, then to the adapter split at services/persistence/records/index.js:5, and read both list implementations. Could not run the falsifier as written, because it needs the running application and this pass may not start one; settled it from the source instead, which is why the falsifier has been rewritten into something readable rather than runnable. Band needs-backend upheld: neither adapter can answer "this user's notifications" because no read accepts an owner. Confidence left at high — the correction rests on read source, and the captured evidence agrees with the stub half of it.
finding.correction: The finding is right that the dashboard is not the user's, and the correction makes it worse rather than better. What was claimed: "The list is built from the journey ids held in the session cookie and nothing else", and that a user returning tomorrow "meets an empty dashboard". What is true: that is the stub adapter's behaviour, and it is what the capture shows — the header names stub.user@example.com and services/persistence/records/stub/lifecycle/read.js:15-23 applies the journeyIds filter. The real adapter ignores the filter entirely. engine/journey.js:113-119 passes journeyIds into records.list, and services/persistence/records/real/lifecycle/read.js:24-39 destructures page, sort, referenceNumber and organisationId and never reads journeyIds, building the query as page, sort and an optional referenceNumber only. So against the real backend the falsifier as written would have fired — a second browser would show the notification — while leaving the finding's substance untouched, because it would show every other trader's notifications too. Two smaller imprecisions, corrected in the slot: the ids are not in the cookie but in the yar server-side store the cookie keys (common/helpers/session-cache/session-cache.js:10-27), which is why they also expire on a TTL; and organisationId at engine/journey.js:101 scopes the address-book lookup used to resolve party names, not the notification list, so it is not a second filter. The frontend slot now states both adapters, and the falsifier now names an observation a reader can make from the source.

relatedTo.why: this one comes first: the statuses DR1 shows change after the session that created the notification has ended, so they cannot be seen at all while the list is session-scoped
